comparator.name: Bachelor Applied Physics
comparator.sourceNotes: Freshly retrieved 2026–2027 Applied Physics after-revision PER, Articles 3.3–3.5 and Appendix 2 pp.72–78, governs this ordinary English full-time programme. All 27 credited positions total 60 + 60 + 60 = 180: core 125 including exact 33BFP final project 15, ITEC 10 and genuine electives 45 (20 year two, 25 year three). No named specialization is required. All taught core units are 5 under the explicit quarter convention; 3SAFE is required noncredit safety training, not an extra 5-EC unit. PPD and first-/second-year challenges are embedded; MyFuture requires value seven without credits, and at least five Studium Generale activities belong within ITEC. Elective space requires examination-board approval and no substantive overlap, at least 30 credits at levels 2/3 including 15 at level 3. The formal requirement list uses current Calculus 2MCALCAP, titled Calculus variant 3, replacing the earlier completed 2WCB0 option for pre-September-2026 students; the pilot appendix prints a different legacy code 2WBB0. These legacy references do not add another course or affect the current 5-credit position. The final project is a 15-credit block in Q4 or another quarter, or spread across two consecutive quarters. Entry requires 120 total, all compulsory first-year components, at least 110 core/ITEC credits and successful 33ACE; Appendix 2 permits meeting these conditions within 15 working days after starting, otherwise continuation stops. Laboratory components and project require successful 3SAFE. Future scheduling remains subject to applicable course conditions. No new UCR judgment is made. Fresh currentPER Art3.7(2):electiveplanapprovalat90earnedECand180plannedEC. NominalQ4projectcanfollowall120nonprojectcore/ITECcreditsincluding33ACE,allY1and3SAFE;no15dayexceptionneeded.

alternatives.concept: Develop mathematical and computational models of dynamical systems through calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, probability, programming, algorithms, image processing, machine learning and robotics. Earth-system modelling, geophysical field and laboratory measurements, wave and materials study, and energy-system assessment connect these methods to physical systems. This related option does not reproduce the full Applied Physics discipline.

alternatives.labelRationale: Six Earth/environmental courses replace six specialist algorithmic courses, producing a substantive natural-system and resource-technology curriculum while keeping quantitative modelling central.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Four courses / 30 EC differ each way. The first retains optimisation, algorithms, computing infrastructure and probabilistic decision models. The second instead develops geological field investigation, aqueous/mineral geochemistry, laboratory recovery/remediation and advanced Earth-resource research. Both retain actual physical measurement and system modelling; their different methodological and natural-science priorities have concrete curricular consequences.

blocks.title: Applied-physics core, experiments, project and open profile

notes.text: The UCR options combine mathematical and computational models with physical-system investigation and sustainable energy or resource applications. They include some wave, mechanical, thermal and materials work, but do not reproduce the full mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, thermodynamics, transport, quantum and condensed-matter sequence, cumulative physics laboratories or compulsory Applied Physics final project.

audience.programmeDescription: Applied Physics combines physical theory, mathematical models and experiments to understand natural phenomena and develop technologies. The curriculum includes mechanics, electromagnetism, optics, quantum and statistical physics, materials and laboratory research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options offer related mathematical modelling, computation, physical-system investigation and energy or resource applications. The first emphasizes algorithms and computational methods alongside physical measurement; the second adds more Earth science, geochemistry and resource laboratory work. Neither reproduces the complete Applied Physics discipline.

curriculum.limitation: Elective selections require approval and must satisfy the programme’s level and non-overlap rules.

componentNotes.33BFP: Required 15 EC final project. Entry requires at least 120 EC, all compulsory first-year study, at least 110 EC of core and ITEC study, completed Advanced Computational and Experimental Skills, and laboratory safety training. The ordinary Q4 start follows the required taught study; other permitted project timing remains subject to these conditions.
componentNotes.31ILS: Laboratory safety training is required before practical participation and adds no credits. The same safety condition applies to data acquisition, experimental automation, advanced experimental skills and the final project.
componentNotes.4CBLW00: Requires completion of previously offered study embedding communication, cooperation, planning and organisation skills.
componentNotes.cp-000273-y2-open: 20 EC of approved elective study in year 2 and 25 EC in year 3. At least 30 EC must be intermediate or advanced, including 15 EC advanced. Content may not overlap. Submit the complete 180 EC plan for approval after earning at least 90 EC; changes also need approval.
componentNotes.0LVX40: Engineering Ethics and Engineering for Society each carry 5 EC. At least five Studium Generale activities are required within ITEC. Personal and professional development and other first- and second-year challenges are embedded; MyFuture activities with a combined value of seven add no credits.
